item.title: These 10 education bills could impact IPS, cafeteria food and school choice
item.description: As Indiana lawmakers near the halfway point of the shortened session, bills tackling cellphone use for kids and creating a new authority for IPS schools are moving through the Statehouse.

item.title: Changes to social media ban bill remove language on curfew for teens
item.description: Indiana lawmakers amended a bill regulating children’s access to social media, removing a proposed overnight curfew for teens while keeping age limits and parental permission requirements.

item.title: Legislators define financial roles for IPS, new Indianapolis education corporation
item.description: An amendment to House Bill 1423 clarifies that existing IPS bond debt will remain with the district rather than transferring to the new Indianapolis Public Education Corporation.

item.title: Ten Commandments could be in schools but not read aloud. Legislation advances
item.description: An Indiana bill that originally required schools to post the Ten Commandments in classrooms advanced out of committee Tuesday after lawmakers significantly rewrote it.

item.title: Nearly half of Indiana's hospitals are operating at a loss. They say they need help
item.description: The “One Big Beautiful Bill” will cut $13 billion to Indiana Hospitals over the next decade. Indiana Hospitals say they are already in trouble.

item.title: Anti-abortion group asks Indiana Supreme Court to release terminated pregnancy reports
item.description: Voices for Life is asking the state’s highest court to revisit a ruling blocking access to abortion records.

item.title: Lawmakers push wave of immigration bills aligned with Trump agenda
item.description: Here's a guide to Indiana’s 2026 immigration bills, including policing, jobs and schools.

item.title: IMPD veteran Tanya Terry is Indianapolis' first female police chief
item.description: Indianapolis Mayor Joe Hogsett appointed Tanya Terry, a 27-year police veteran, as IMPD’s new Chief of Police.

item.title: Ryan Mears announces reelection bid for county prosecutor
item.description: Ryan Mears has taken himself off the short list of potential successors to Mayor Joe Hogsett — at least for now.

item.title: Bill creates in-person checks for Department of Child Services following death of Indianapolis five-year-old
item.description: Lamakers unanimously moved a bill forward requiring in person checks for the Department of Child Services before they can close out alleged cases of abuse and neglect. The bill is in response to the death of an Indianapolis five-year-old.
